video.title: Claude Code Works Better With Loops, Not Prompts
video.rationale: Covers: topic ✓ (0:00–2:13), CO3.LO1 ✓ (0:00–11:07) [from transcript] · Eric Tech · tier 4 · 11:29 · 17,813 views · captions
video.description:
Loop engineering is the shift the creators of Claude Code and OpenClaw made when they stopped prompting their agents — and I was running it in real workflows before it had a name. Here's what loop engineering is, how it works, and how I build self-correcting agentic loops in Claude Code.

Key takeaways:
- What loop engineering is: a self-correcting orchestrator → executioner → reviewer loop that iterates until your goal is met
- The 6 building blocks of a reliable agentic loop: trigger, worktree, skills, connectors, memory, sub-agents
- Using GitHub Issues as the memory/state layer so every iteration is logged and resumable
- Loopmaker: the portable Claude skill I built to scaffold a verifie

video.title: Loop Engineering in 8 Minutes: The Complete Visual Guide to AI Agent Loops
video.rationale: Covers: topic ✓ (5:07–8:18), CO3.LO1 ✓ (5:07–7:19) [from transcript] · Tech Explainer · tier 4 · 8:19 · 6 views · captions
video.description:
"Don't prompt your agents. Design loops that prompt them." The people building the best AI coding agents have stopped typing one prompt at a time. Now they design the loop the agent runs inside. That skill is called loop engineering.

This animated explainer starts from the basics and works up. We go from prompt engineering to context engineering to loop engineering, then follow one real example (a customer support agent handling a refund) through every pass of the loop. After that we cover the parts that decide whether an agent holds up in production: stopping conditions, harness engineering, context rot, and verification.

In this video:
✅ Prompt → context → loop engineering: why the skill

review.review: Breaks down production loop exits, state management, and nested architectural loops. Very informative.
